The service abstraction exposes these decisions as controllable management functions for privacy-aware model training in network and service management systems. Theoretical analysis confirms convergence rates comparable to FedAvg, and extensive experiments on CIFAR-10 and Fashion-MNIST demonstrate its effectiveness. On CIFAR-10 CNN, DP-MRaaS achieves$57.78\pm 0.51\%$accuracy under IID, matching FedAvg (57.78%) while preserving$(\epsilon,\delta) = (3.5,10^{-5})$privacy. On CIFAR-10 ResNet-18, DP-MRaaS attains$66.57\pm 0.54\%$(IID) and$61.30\pm 0.30\%$(Balanced Non-IID), competitive with FedAvg-DP (66.70%, 61.84%) and Ditto-DP (66.86%, 61.76%). On Fashion-MNIST, DP-MRaaS achieves$90.52\pm 0.10\%$(IID) and$90.02\pm 0.07\%$(Balanced Non-IID), the highest among DP-enabled methods. A five-way ablation study confirms that recombination is the primary accuracy driver (+8.6% on ResNet-18), while adaptive DP preserves utility with < 0.1% degradation on CNN. These results show that DP-MRaaS achieves a superior balance between accuracy, stability, and privacy, advancing the trustability of FL for service management in next-generation networks.
10.1109/tccn.2026.3705803: The high mobility and heterogeneity of Vehicular Networks (VANETs) impose significant challenges for edge caching and resource optimization, as rapidly changing topologies and diverse content demands hinder real-time responsiveness. To address these issues, we propose an integrated optimization framework combining dynamic clustering, popularity prediction, and joint caching-trajectory control. Firstly, we design a location-interest-based dynamic vehicle clustering mechanism that groups vehicles according to communication reachability and semantic content similarity, forming stable and service-oriented clusters. Secondly, a hierarchical asynchronous federated prediction model is developed to aggregate local cluster pReferences with global request trends, achieving timely, accurate, and privacy-aware popularity estimation. Finally, we construct a Dual-Agent Collaborative Caching and Trajectory Optimization (DACTCO) framework, where a Dueling Double Deep Q-Network (D3QN) agent governs UAV-assisted caching decisions while a Deep Deterministic Policy Gradient (DDPG) agent adapts UAV positions. Through a unified scalarized reward, the two agents jointly minimize average delay and energy consumption in a coordinated manner. Simulation results demonstrate that the proposed framework significantly enhances service quality and resource efficiency, achieving reductions of up to 6.3% in average delay, 42% in average energy consumption, and improvements of up to 36.2% in cache hit rate compared with state-of-the-art baselines.
10.1109/tce.2026.3706323: Federated Learning (FL) operates over non-IID client data with heterogeneous distributions and quality, which complicates convergence and makes it hard to distinguish benign irregularities from malicious behavior. FL is increasingly adopted to train edge digital twins (DTs). Healthcare applications such as CVD risk prediction across hospital networks demand both privacy preservation and model integrity, making poisoning resilience critical. Attackers can inject or compromise clients to submit manipulated updates that poison the global model, either untargeted with widespread degradation or targeted via backdoors that misclassify trigger inputs while preserving overall accuracy. DT-FL must protect privacy, preserve integrity, and resist adaptive poisoning where attackers adjust updates after observing global models and defenses. Existing defenses rely mainly on robust aggregation and often assume few adversaries, abundant attack evidence per round, or access to a clean validation set. They also overlook the dynamics of early training phases where small degradations can cause lasting harm. We propose a Privacy-Preserving Federated Digital Twin (PP-FedDT) framework that secures federated digital twin learning using private bounded updates, verifiable update compliance, and DT-assisted participant screening. Each client clips and noise-perturbs its local update, then submits a cryptographic commitment alongside a zero-knowledge proof certifying norm boundedness, encoding validity, and commitment correctness. At the edge, digital twin metadata and update similarity graphs are analyzed to detect Sybil or colluding participants, and suspicious contributions are removed prior to aggregation. The remaining updates are aggregated robustly using parameter-level trimming and adaptive weighting to suppress abnormal coordinate values. Influence is then monitored across rounds to regulate or exclude persistently harmful clients, maintaining correctness, privacy, and resistance to adaptive poisoning. Experiments on standard benchmarks show improved robustness, stability, and accuracy over FedAvg, Krum, Trimmed mean and Median.
10.1109/tcss.2026.3700809: Effective hate speech detection is paramount for maintaining safe computational social systems, yet it faces challenges from data scarcity in low-resource languages and privacy concerns. Federated few-shot learning (FFSL) addresses these by enabling collaborative model training across distributed clients with limited labeled data. However, FFSL remains vulnerable to backdoor attacks where malicious clients inject triggers to manipulate model predictions, allowing toxic content to evade detection filters. To the best of our knowledge, no prior work has examined backdoor defenses for FFSL in multilingual hate speech detection. To address this unexplored gap, we propose gradient anomaly aware robust defense (GARD), a novel defense framework that combines gradient-based anomaly detection with robust aggregation to protect multilingual hate speech detection models against backdoor attacks. First, GARD performs gradient analysis using adaptive interquartile range (IQR)-based magnitude and similarity thresholds to filter anomalous updates. Then, it applies coordinatewise median aggregation over the remaining benign clients. We evaluate GARD against three backdoor attacks: BadNets, InsertSent, and Layerwise Weight Poisoning (LWP), on Hindi, Spanish, and German datasets using Multilingual Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (mBERT) and Multilingual Distilled Bidirectional Encoder Representations from Transformers (mDistilBERT) models in 5-shot and 10-shot configurations under independent and identically distributed (IID) and non- IID settings at poisoning rates of 0.2% and 0.3%. Experimental results demonstrate that GARD reduces attack success rates while maintaining clean accuracy across all configurations, with stronger defense observed in 10-shot settings. These findings validate GARD as an effective defense mechanism generalizable across languages and attack modalities, ensuring the integrity and safety of automated moderation in federated scenarios.
10.1109/tcomm.2026.3706586: Due to constraints in network capacity and coverage, conventional ground-based infrastructures face difficulties in delivering low-latency and high-reliability caching capabilities to users and Internet of Things (IoT) devices located in remote regions, including mountains and oceans. The Space-Air-Ground Integrated Network (SAGIN), envisioned as a foundational structure for 6G communication systems and integrated with Mobile Edge Computing (MEC), can offer a promising solution to efficiently serve the caching demands of users in such underserved locations. Nevertheless, the high heterogeneity and time-varying nature of SAGIN, along with the continuous evolution of the popularity of user requested content, which presents substantial challenges to achieve satisfactory cache hit ratios and low access latency. In this paper, we introduce a novel three-tier edge collaborative caching architecture comprising satellites, Uncrewed Aerial Vehicle (UAV) clusters, and ground edge servers. We formulate the cache replacement task as a Markov Decision Process (MDP). To address concerns over user privacy and heterogeneous local model performance, we propose a Federated Discrete Soft Actor-Critic (FDSAC) approach that employs an attention mechanism guided by server activity levels to adaptively weight client models during parameters aggregation. Additionally, a content popularity prediction module based on Bidirectional Long Short-Term Memory (BiLSTM) is embedded within the DSAC agent to derive the optimal cache replacement decisions. Experimental evaluations indicate that the FDSAC achieves superior performance compared to other baseline algorithms in terms of both cache hit rate and content retrieval delay.
10.1109/tce.2026.3706747: Intelligent consumer electronics—smartphones, wearables, and IoT gateways—generate massive personal data at the network edge, driving demand for privacy-preserving collaborative intelligence. Federated edge learning (FEL) integrates federated learning (FL) with mobile edge computing (MEC) to enable distributed model training without exposing raw data. However, centralized FEL imposes prohibitive communication overhead when users are dispersed across multiple edge servers, while decentralized FEL suffers from degraded model accuracy due to limited local aggregation. Both paradigms ignore the fundamental asymmetry between mobile devices, which are resource-limited and intermittently available, and edge servers (ESs), which are fixed and resource-rich. To address this limitation, we propose coalition federated edge learning (CFEL), a framework that partitions users into ES-led coalitions where each ES serves as the coalition leader responsible for model aggregation and payment distribution. We model the incentive mechanism within each coalition as a one-to-many concurrent bargaining game (OCBG) and derive a closed-form Nash Bargaining Solution (NBS) that yields a principled, equal-surplus-sharing payment allocation grounded in MEC-specific communication and aggregation costs. Federated learning experiments on Fashion-MNIST and UCI-HAR demonstrate that CFEL achieves 89.24% accuracy on Fashion-MNIST (vs. 86.47% for decentralized FEL) and 90.80% on UCI-HAR (vs. 84.47% for decentralized FEL), while reducing distance-weighted communication cost by 68% compared with centralized FEL. Under non-IID data, periodic cross-coalition synchronization enables CFEL to surpass baselines on both datasets (82.66% on HAR, 81.44% on Fashion-MNIST). NBS payment allocation is further verified feasible and incentive-compatible under realistic MEC cost parameters. These results demonstrate that CFEL offers a favorable accuracy–communication trade-off for resource-constrained consumer electronics deployments. Source code is available at https://github.com/hl5w/CoalitionFederated-Edge-Learning.
10.1109/tce.2026.3706365: Although consumer electronics have enabled the rapid deployment of low cost cotton apical bud recognition systems these traditional centralized terminals face critical privacy and cybersecurity risks notably their vulnerability to adversarial visual deception in open farmlands. To address these issues a novel decentralized framework integrating swarm intelligence with federated adversarial learning named Fed-Cotton-Guard is proposed. First a peer-to-peer swarm architecture is established enabling edge devices to collaboratively train without sharing raw physical images. Second through the introduction of a Min Max game mechanism edge nodes are empowered to proactively generate and defend against adversarial perturbations locally thereby achieving proactive threat hunting. Furthermore a detection strategy based on parameter distribution residuals is designed to proactively intercept malicious parameter poisoning within the decentralized network. Extensive experiments on resource constrained hardware platforms such as the Jetson Nano demonstrate that Fed-Cotton-Guard maintains a high detection accuracy of 96.5% while effectively resisting various adversarial attacks including FGSM and PGD, compared to existing methods this framework significantly enhances collaborative fault tolerance and communication efficiency providing a highly robust.
10.1109/tce.2026.3706519: Consumer Internet of Things (IoT) networks are vulnerable to complex online attacks due to their distributed architecture, but privacy regulations outlaw centralized security strategies. Current Federated Learning (FL) considers intrusion detection as static classification, whereas deception systems do not have strategic coordination against adaptive adversaries. We propose a Game-Theoretic Federated Deception (GFD) architecture, which combines FL with dynamic deception via Nash equilibrium-based coordination in privacy-preserving distributed cyber defense. The two-phase architecture decouples the establishment of detection foundations (Phase 1: federated neural network training) and strategic coordination (Phase 2: gametheoretic deception optimization), allowing continuous adaptation to be achieved without retraining models. Evaluation on 3.6M TON_IoT samples has shown 95.78% accuracy and 98.86% recall with a detection miss rate of 1.14% and a deception success rate of 60.6% on adaptive attackers. The framework exhibits scalability of 5-50 federated nodes (performance variation less than ±0.0071%) with linear communication scaling, 255 times communication reduction (0.28 KB/round) with complete model exchange. Ablation analysis gives a privacy cost of 2.41% accuracy degradation, and deception gives the highest performance gain (+3.37% F1-score). The coordinated defense of the exploitation of lateral movement is proven by zero spatial compromise in all experiments. The article provides the premises of adaptive, privacy-aware security in distributed consumer IoT settings against intelligent adversaries.
10.1109/tce.2026.3706981: Federated learning (FL) enables hospitals to collaboratively train medical image segmentation models without sharing raw patient data. However, transmitting full model updates in each communication round incurs prohibitive bandwidth costs, particularly in resource-constrained clinical networks.We propose CIWGS-FedMed, a Channel-Importance-Weighted Gradient Sparsification framework. Its primary contribution is a Grad-CAM-inspired channel importance scorer that allocates the per-layer transmission budget proportionally to EMA-smoothed channel activation–gradient products. This enables structured compression that respects the information hierarchy of convolutional feature maps, representing a structural departure from prior unstructured Top-k methods. Three additional components complement the scorer. First, a hyperparameter-light, architecture-aware, layer-adaptive sparsity schedule that protects task-critical early and decoder layers while aggressively compressing the bottle-neck. Second, exponential moving average (EMA) stabilisation of importance scores across mini-batches, which suppresses single-batch gradient noise. Third, a clipped error-feedback residual mechanism, auto-scaled to the median absolute parameter-delta magnitude, which prevents gradient explosion while recovering discarded information across rounds. Experiments on a non-IID synthetic medical dataset with five heterogeneous hospital clients demonstrate that CIWGS-FedMed significantly reduces communication cost while maintaining strong segmentation performance, achieving 78.5% reduction in total communication, relative to uncompressed FedAvg and 14.1% reduction compared to fixed-ratio magnitude-based sparsification. Importantly, the uplink ratio self-reduces from 6.4% in round 1 to 5.2% in round 30 as importance scores concentrate, without any manual scheduling.
10.1109/tccn.2026.3707524: Low earth orbit (LEO) satellite networks have emerged as a key enabler for delivering real-time and global services to distributed terrestrial nodes, particularly in remote regions. To preserve data privacy, federated learning (FL) provides a decentralized framework for advancing artificial intelligence (AI) in complex tasks. However, the efficiency of FL is constrained by high and imbalanced energy consumption, which limits its practical deployment. To address these challenges, an energy-aware FL framework that integrates knowledge distillation (KD) with task offloading is proposed, where KD is performed at both the FL server and client devices or direct-connected satellites using public datasets. The energy consumption balancing problem is formulated as a quadratic unconstrained binary optimization (QUBO) model. To achieve computational efficiency and parallelism, the quantum approximate optimization algorithm (QAOA) is employed to solve the problem with both the mixing and cost Hamiltonians derived and the corresponding quantum circuit designed. In a FL framework over a LEO satellite network comprising 40 satellites and 10 FL clients, the proposed method reduces energy consumption by approximately 26.4%, achieves improved energy balance with a weighted variance of approximately 4.93 and maintains high accuracy of 0.95 in a vehicle classification task, compared with the traditional FL method.
10.1109/tce.2026.3707898: Breast cancer remains the most commonly diagnosed cancer among women worldwide, with early-stage detection improving five-year survival rates to over 90%. Despite advances in artificial intelligence and consumer electronics for home-based healthcare monitoring, security and privacy concerns remain barriers to widespread adoption for sensitive medical applications like breast cancer diagnosis. Given that access to regular screening remains limited in many communities due to infrastructure and cost constraints, this paper introduces MediChain-FSL, a blockchain-integrated federated semi-supervised learning system for secure breast cancer assessment using smart home healthcare devices and wearable sensors. MediChain-FSL addresses data scarcity and privacy preservation through decentralized learning, where blockchain ensures immutable audit trails and secure multi-party computation while federated semi-supervised learning exploits limited expert-labeled data and abundant unlabeled sensor data from consumer electronics. Our framework employs a blockchain-validated quality-aware aggregation protocol combined with homomorphic encryption and differential privacy mechanisms for consensus-based model aggregation, preventing poisoning attacks and ensuring data integrity across distributed IoT devices, including smart mirrors, thermal imaging systems, and biometric wearables. The semi-supervised component combines consistency regularization under stochastic augmentations with confidence-based pseudo-labeling to exploit abundant unlabeled sensor data. Experimental evaluation using a combined multi-modal dataset of 3,800 samples derived from three distinct data sources spanning clinical, thermal, and biosignal modalities demonstrates 93.4% classification accuracy with 54% communication reduction and sub-180ms latency on resource-constrained devices. The system achieves 98.7% of maximum performance using only 5% labeled data, maintains over 90% accuracy under 20% Byzantine attacks with formal differential privacy guarantees, and successfully detected seven early-stage cancer cases during field deployment across 45 smart home environments.
10.1109/tce.2026.3709974: Federated learning (FL) is a key enabling technology for privacy-preserving intelligent applications in resource-constrained consumer electronics. However, its distributed training paradigm exposes the global model to highly stealthy and destructive backdoor attacks. Existing defenses either rely on additional clean data, impose non-negligible computational burdens on clients, or lack robustness in dynamic participation scenarios, making them unsuitable for lightweight consumer devices. To address these challenges, we propose FedULBD, a server-side lightweight backdoor defense framework driven by random unlearning. First, FedULBD leverages the response characteristics of model updates under random unlearning and constructs anomaly indicators through a two-layer standardization process combining intra-layer normalization with cross-client normalization. Without relying on any clean data or introducing additional computation on clients, this yields unified anomaly indicators that stably characterize client abnormality under complex training scenarios. Second, to enhance robustness in dynamic participation settings, FedULBD builds upon these anomaly indicators by integrating a binary clustering mechanism with historical behavior tracking, enabling stable and effective defense even when client participation continuously changes. Finally, a z-score-guided soft-weighted aggregation strategy is introduced to suppress abnormal updates while preserving beneficial contributions, thereby promoting stable model convergence. Extensive experimental results demonstrate that FedULBD substantially suppresses backdoor attacks while maintaining high benign-task accuracy across multiple datasets, attack types, and dynamic participation settings.
10.1109/tccn.2026.3710545: As embodied intelligence emerges as a core paradigm in Agentic AI, which enables embodied agents to collaboratively perceive through cross-party modeling, ensuring privacy preservation among distributed parties becomes increasingly critical. Vertical Federated Learning (VFL) enables privacy-preserving collaborative modeling by sharing parameters while keeping data local, yet gradient exchange still leaks informative signals that enable Feature Inference Attacks (FIA), where the attacker infers the private features of other participants, raising serious privacy threats for embodied intelligence. However, existing FIA attacks either ignore the vulnerabilities of passive parties as attackers or assume that passive parties have access to global information, which is unrealistic. To bridge this gap, we take the first step by introducing a novel feature inference attack BlackFIA, aiming to unveil potential vulnerabilities in which the passive party reconstructs private features from locally available data and exchanged gradients, without any global information. To mitigate this privacy risk, we further propose BlackFIA${}_{defense}$, an adaptive differentially private training mechanism that emphasizes protection for high-risk samples and regulates noise intensity to preserve predictive utility. Extensive experiments across tabular and image datasets show that BlackFIA achieves stronger reconstruction quality and higher attack success rate than baselines, while remaining computationally practical during training. More importantly, BlackFIA${}_{defense}$consistently degrades attack success rate to about 55%, and maintains the global model accuracy at about 75% under a strict privacy budget, providing a stronger privacy-utility trade-off than standard DP-SGD based defenses.
10.1109/tce.2026.3710525: The industrial consumer field integrates industrial production with financial consumption, aiming to focus on the entire process of the consumption system, with comprehensive data analysis conducted across multiple institutions. Vertical federated learning is a vital component for distributed collaborative data analysis. It allows parties to integrate sample features from all parties while maintaining privacy and conduct comprehensive model training. This paper focuses on vertical federated learning in the industrial consumer field and proposes a vertical federated learning framework for factory economic prediction. In this framework, a factory institution collaborates with multiple consumer institutions to perform vertical federated learning, train a predictive model, and determine whether a factory institution is operating normally. We design a privacy-preserving (t,n)-threshold private set intersection protocol to achieve sample alignment for this framework. This protocol aligns sample data from all parties while protecting their privacy. It also introduces a weighting mechanism to accommodate missing sample data for some non-critical parties. We implement the proposed vertical federated learning framework and conduct a comprehensive security analysis. Evaluation results demonstrate that our private sample alignment protocol performs well, and the predictive model derived from vertical federated learning is highly accurate and practical.
10.1109/tpami.2026.3747377: Federated Learning (FL) is fundamentally challenged by statistical heterogeneity, where non-identically distributed (non-IID) data induces "client drift" that severely hampers global convergence. While existing approaches attempt to mitigate this drift through spatial-domain gradient correction or regularization, they overlook the intrinsic spectral structure of optimization signals. In this work, we revisit client drift from a frequency-domain perspective and empirically observe a "Spectral Bias of Drift": in the evaluated training trajectories, a disproportionate fraction of inter-client gradient disagreement is concentrated in the lower-frequency bands of the adopted structured parameter layout. Motivated by this observation, we propose SpecGradFilter, which suppresses a small low-frequency portion of selected layer gradients and can be implemented using an FFT-based projection or spatial-domain detrending approximations. For the FFT-based realization, we establish a conditional convergence guarantee when the projection retains sufficient global descent signal and the post-filtering client heterogeneity is bounded. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10/100, Tiny-ImageNet, and additional benchmarks show improved accuracy and time-to-target in the tested non-IID settings without increasing the per-round communication payload.
10.1109/tce.2026.3711046: Women’s mental health across the hormonal lifecycle remains critically underserved by consumer health systems that neither account for lifecycle-specific symptom phenomenology nor preserve clinical data privacy. We present FEDLIFELLM, a lifecycle-aware federated learning framework that fine-tunes an 8B-parameter instruction-tuned LLM via 4-bit QLoRA across three biologically-motivated silos—Menstrual, Perinatal, and Menopausal—for simultaneous mental health condition classification and risk severity stratification, without raw patient data leaving the device perimeter. The proposed Tri-Defense Mechanism jointly addresses federated convergence instability (Step-Bounded FedProx), the privacy-utility imbalance of uniform noise (Lifecycle-Proportionate Privacy Noise), and rare-class gradient suppression (Clinical Cost-Weighted Cross-Entropy Loss). Stage-Adaptive LoRA rank allocation further compensates for data-scarce silos by assigning greater representational capacity to smaller cohorts. On LifeMH-FL, a newly constructed 111,299-record lifecycle-stratified corpus, FEDLIFELLM attains 79% condition classification accuracy (macro-F1 0.740 ± 0.001) and 80% risk severity accuracy (macro-F1 0.765 ± 0.003), averaged over three seeds on a held-out set of 22,239 records, with 0.77 precision on suicidal ideation—surpassing the closest prior federated mental-health framework and centralized training on both tasks, within 20 communication rounds that transmit less than 0.1% of full model parameters. Ablations confirm that lifecycle-stage prompting is the dominant contributor (+0.040 macro-F1,p−68) and that proportionate DP recovers most of the utility uniform DP sacrifices, while membership-inference and gradient-inversion analyses indicate the per-silo noise affords empirical privacy at negligible utility cost. These results provide preliminary evidence for a privacy-preserving, precision-oriented screening aid suited to on-device consumer women’s-health applications—e.g., cycle-tracking and perinatal-care apps on smartphones and wearables, where sensitive data never leaves the user’s device.
10.1109/tdsc.2026.3711273: Federated learning (FL), as a distributed machine learning paradigm, enables model training without data leaving local devices, but it is highly vulnerable to backdoor attacks. Attackers can manipulate the global model to output attacker-specified results by embedding backdoor triggers during the FL training phase. Most existing defense methods have limited defensive capabilities due to their excessive reliance on the assumption that backdoor updates are significantly different from benign updates in the parameter space. To address this issue, we propose LBC-Guardian, a learning behavior consistency-based backdoor defense method that leverages the impact of backdoor attacks on clean models to achieve effective defense. Specifically, we first propose an instantaneous state consistency evaluation mechanism that identifies malicious updates within each round by probing their functional impact on a server-side reference dataset. We then design a historical trend consistency gating mechanism that captures cross-round behavioral anomalies to suppress stealthy attackers that evade single-round detection. Finally, based on these two consistency measures, each client is assigned a score to enable robust weighted aggregation. Experimental results across various datasets demonstrate that LBC-Guardian achieves superior defensive performance against diverse backdoor attacks compared to existing state-of-the-art defense methods. In particular, it demonstrates strong robustness against adaptive attacks with full knowledge of the defense mechanism.
10.1109/tvt.2026.3712217: Over-the-air computation (AirComp) has been studied in hierarchical federated learning (HFL) to enable efficient model aggregation by integrating communication and computation, thereby alleviating uplink communication bottlenecks. However, in AirComp-based HFL systems, channel fading, CSI-estimation errors, and receiver noise inevitably introduce aggregation errors. In addition, such systems still face challenges such as user mobility and non-independent and identically distributed (Non-IID) data, both of which can degrade global model performance. To overcome these challenges, we propose MC-AirCompFL, a multi-cell hierarchical FL framework that performs intra-cell aggregation via AirComp and inter-cell aggregation at the cloud. We first derive a system-level convergence upper bound that explicitly captures the impact of AirComp-induced aggregation errors, imperfect CSI, and label-distribution-skewed Non-IID data. Then, we formulate a joint optimization problem for receive scaling at base stations (BSs), transmit-power control at user equipments (UEs), and UE-BS association to minimize the convergence-guided objective and the cell-level label-distribution distance to the IID reference. Furthermore, a Lyapunov drift-plus-penalty-based causal online algorithm is developed to enforce long-term constraints through virtual queues and achieve per-round causal optimization. Numerical results on MNIST and CIFAR-10 demonstrate that the proposed scheme improves learning performance over benchmark schemes while maintaining communication-efficiency and long-term energy-control advantages.
10.1109/tce.2026.3712453: Federated learning (FL) represents a machine learning that enhances privacy preservation by enabling model training to occur directly on individual devices, with only parameter gradients being transmitted rather than the underlying raw datasets. However, it remains vulnerable to various malicious attacks, including model tampering attack and forgery attack launched by malicious clients. These attacks could compromise the parameters of client and damage trained model. To address these challenges, we propose an efficient probabilistic batch-authenticated FL (PBAFL) scheme. Firstly, we design a lightweight digital signature scheme with aggregation capability to achieve integrity authentication of the gradients submitted by the clients. Secondly, we propose a probabilistic batch authentication scheme that achieves 99% accuracy by authenticating only a small portion of the signatures, significantly improving authentication efficiency. We implement a prototype system of the PBAFL scheme for privacy and security proof analysis, conducting comprehensive experiments on MNIST datasets. Experimental results demonstrate that our proposed PBAFL model substantially reduces batch authentication time and communication overhead compared to existing approaches.
10.1109/tce.2026.3712443: Consumer AI agents increasingly rely on persistent long-term memory to support personalization, contextual continuity, and multi-step task execution, but this memory also creates a new attack surface in which memory poisoning can occur through malicious memory insertion, misleading memory updates, retrieval manipulation, or latent records that later induce reasoning errors. Existing studies have examined agent privacy leakage, retrieval corruption, and federated robustness, yet they rarely address the specific problem of forecasting whether a newly written memory record will trigger future reasoning deviation, measured as an observable divergence between the agent’s later reasoning trace and a benign reference trajectory, under privacy-sensitive and heterogeneous deployment settings. To address this gap, this paper proposes FEMP-GUARD, a privacy-preserving federated early-warning framework for long-horizon memory poisoning in consumer AI agents. The proposed method models poisoning risk as a retrieval-conditioned temporal forecasting task, where each client locally encodes memory-writing events, retrieval dynamics, and behavioral context, and then participates in privacy-preserving personalized federated optimization without sharing raw memory traces. The predicted warning score is further coupled with local mitigation through write-time quarantine and retrieval-time reweighting. Experiments on four benchmarks, namely MIMIC-III, eICU, WebShop, and MMLU, show that FEMP-GUARD consistently outperforms representative federated baselines, achieving the best AUC, F1, Precision, Recall, and Early Warning Rate while also producing earlier warnings and favorable security–utility trade-offs. These results demonstrate that retrieval-conditioned federated early warning provides an effective and practical defense paradigm for protecting memory-augmented consumer AI agents against slow and stealthy poisoning behaviors.
10.1109/tccn.2026.3712137: Semi-Asynchronous Federated Learning (SAFL) takes advantage of both synchronous and asynchronous FLs to train models. However, existing works in semi-asynchronous FLs fail to fully account for heterogeneities in both data and devices. To address these issues, we first propose a Clustered SAFL (CSAFL) framework and theoretically analyze its convergence loss. Then, a convergence loss minimization problem is formulated under the considerations of heterogeneities in device resources, fairness of cluster selection, and data heterogeneity. To address this complex problem due to nonlinearities and multi-dimensional decision variables, we first design a device clustering algorithm based on both devices’ model parameter differences and gradient directions between local and global models. Then, the original loss minimization problem is transformed into inter- and intra-cluster selection problems. For the inter-cluster selection problem, to ensure fairness, we propose a reinforcement learning-driven Lyapunov approach to fairly select clusters, where reinforcement learning (RL) is used to supervise the cluster selection results by the Lyapunov method. For the intra-cluster selection, we convert it into a constrained multi-armed bandit (MAB) problem in order to let devices within a cluster submit models synchronously. Then, a two-stage Upper Confidence Bound (UCB) scheme is proposed to obtain device selection results. Extensive numerical results with baselines show that our approach achieves up to 25% higher accuracy.
10.1109/tccn.2026.3713348: With the rapid development of artificial intelligence and low-earth orbit (LEO) satellite edge computing technology, there has been a rapid increase in the demand for intelligence networks and services among users in remote areas, such as federated learning (FL). We propose a satellite aided computation FL (SACFL) system in LEO ubiquitous edge computing (UEC) networks, aiming at improving the efficiency of FL tasks in remote areas. In the considered deployment scenario, the following key factors are considered: 1) terrestrial users in remote areas; 2) offloading data to satellites for aided computation; and 3) global aggregation on satellite. However, the highly dynamic characteristics and the uneven distribution of satellite computation resources pose significant challenges to the low-delay requirements of satellite-based FL tasks. To this end, we formulate an optimization problem to minimize delay by jointly considering access selection, computation offloading, aggregation satellite (AgS) selection, and computation resource allocation. To solve the formulated problem, we propose a novel multi-agent alternating (M2A) optimization method. Specifically, three independent agents are trained alternately to make decisions on access selection, computation offloading, and AgS selection. Comprehensive simulations demonstrate that the proposed method outperforms other benchmark algorithms in terms of convergence, delay, and FL accuracy.
10.1109/tccn.2026.3740672: Agentic AI systems are reshaping communications and networking by deploying autonomous intelligent agents capable of collaborative learning while maintaining data privacy at network edges. Within distributed network environments, Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs) serve as cognitive engines for edge devices, yet federated fine-tuning faces substantial challenges in balancing global knowledge aggregation with local adaptation under heterogeneous network conditions. Conventional federated protocols typically rely on uniform parameter aggregation, which conflates domain-invariant features with client-specific nuances, thereby resulting in suboptimal personalization and excessive communication overhead. To address these challenges, we propose PFAdapter, a communication-efficient framework introducing hierarchical LoRA decomposition to explicitly separate adapter parameters into global-shared and local-private components. Query and key projections are assigned to global synchronization for capturing universal multimodal semantics across the network, while value and output projections remain localized for edge-specific adaptation. Additionally, orthogonality regularization based on the Frobenius norm enforces strict separation between these components, preventing redundant feature learning. Selective aggregation protocols synchronize only global-shared components across the federated network, preserving local expertise and reducing communication costs by nearly 50%. Extensive experiments on VQA-RAD, SLAKE, Hateful Memes, and CrisisMMD datasets demonstrate that PFAdapter consistently outperforms state-of-the-art baselines, achieving accuracy improvements ranging from 2.4% to 4.8% across diverse edge intelligence tasks. Consequently, our framework establishes an efficient solution for agentic AI deployment in resource-constrained communication networks.
10.1109/tdsc.2026.3714046: Federated learning enables collaborative model training without exposing raw data, making it well-suited for privacy-sensitive time-series applications. Yet its effectiveness is limited by the scarcity of labeled client data and the substantial heterogeneity across clients. Federated source-free domain adaptation (F-SFDA) alleviates this limitation by allowing the server to pretrain a model on labeled source data while requiring clients to adapt locally using only their unlabeled target data. However, the success of F-SFDA critically depends on the quality of client-side adaptation, which is difficult to ensure under heterogeneous temporal distributions and often leads to noisy updates, client drift, and unstable global convergence. To address these, this work proposes Temporal-augmented sOurce-free Domain Adaptation (TODA), a plug-and-play method designed to provide secure and robust adaptation for federated time-series learning. TODA follows a federated dual-stage design: the server first learns transferable temporal structures from source data, and clients subsequently use these frozen structures as priors to guide source-free adaptation with only local unlabeled data. Two complementary temporal modules are introduced to capture essential time-series characteristics, enabling comprehensive modeling of long-term dependency and temporal proximity. By enforcing temporal structural consistency during client adaptation, TODA mitigates client drift and enhances the security and stability of global aggregation under shifting temporal distributions. Extensive experiments demonstrate that TODA consistently improves adaptation performance, outperforming baselines by up to 36.24% in average accuracy and 39.34% in average macro F1-score. Combining TODA with the F-SFDA frameworks significantly enhances their safety and robustness.
10.1109/tce.2026.3714666: Consumer-facing kidney cancer diagnostics encounter persistent challenges, including privacy risk, data scarcity, and limited model transparency, which undermine trustworthiness in healthcare systems. This paper presents KidneyGuard-FedXAI, a trustworthy federated and explainable AI framework that integrates proactive defense against adversarial threats and privacy-preserving protocols for secure kidney cancer detection in consumer applications. The framework employs differential privacy-enhanced federated learning with gradient compression, adversarial training, and LIME-based explainability and supports cyber threat analysis to ensure robust, interpretable, and privacy-compliant diagnostics. Gradient compression reduces communication overhead while preserving feature-level information critical for LIME-based local explanations, thereby jointly enhancing both efficiency and diagnostic interpretability. Our approach addresses critical gaps in current kidney cancer detection systems by providing consumer-accessible explanations while maintaining data sovereignty across distributed healthcare institutions. Experimental validation on multi-institutional kidney datasets demonstrates superior performance with 94.7% accuracy, 92.3% sensitivity, and 96.1% specificity, while ensuring privacy preservation with ϵ-differential privacy guarantees. The framework reduces communication overhead by 67% compared to conventional federated approaches and provides clinically meaningful explanations with 89.2% physician agreement scores. Overall, KidneyGuard-FedXAI advances trustworthy consumer applications by uniting privacy preservation, explainability, and proactive defense for kidney cancer diagnostics in distributed healthcare environments.
10.1109/tce.2026.3714729: The integration of intelligent consumer electronics into FemTech offers unprecedented opportunities for personalized oncology. However, deploying multimodal wearable systems to monitor treatment responses in specific molecular subtypes, such as RAS/RAF-wildtype colorectal cancer (CRC) in women, requires stringent privacy safeguards and clinical interpretability on edge devices. This paper presents ExplainCRC, an edge-deployable, privacy-preserving consumer wearable framework tailored for the efficacy stratification of female patients with RAS/RAF-wildtype CRC. ExplainCRC fuses consumer-grade sensor streams—photoplethysmography (PPG), electrodermal activity (EDA), skin temperature, and acceleration—into a unified representation using a multilayered attention encoder network. To establish trust with clinical experts and female patients, we employ layer-wise relevance propagation (LRP) to quantify the temporal contributions of each sensor stream to health outcome predictions. Addressing the critical privacy demands of women’s health data, the system leverages federated learning secured by a Gaussian differential privacy mechanism (ϵ = 2.8, δ = 10−5). Furthermore, we developed a mixed-precision model compression pipeline optimizing ExplainCRC for seamless execution on mobile platforms. Extensive evaluations across three public datasets—WESAD, PPG-DaLiA, and TCGA-COAD (utilizing genomic features as static surrogates for outcomes in a 3-category scheme)—demonstrate robust performance. Explain-CRC achieves a high explanation fidelity (0.867 and 0.843 on the two wearable benchmarks; 0.863 averaged across all three), and its throughput on a mid-range mobile platform reaches 21.4 frames per second for the compressed model (12.8 FPS for the full model), a 1.67× latency reduction relative to its own uncompressed counterpart. These technical results motivate, but do not yet establish, a path toward home-based monitoring of targeted-therapy responses, which will require dedicated clinical data collection and validation.
10.1109/tce.2026.3714462: The proliferation of Internet of Things (IoT) networks has increased the importance of effective task offloading techniques that provide better tradeoffs between energy efficiency, latency, and trust. Current task offloading techniques are mostly based on static scheduling and control, which are not effective in responding to dynamic network environments and are more prone to manipulation attacks in distributed IoT networks. This article proposesTwinChain, a five-stage framework that combines DT-based predictive simulation with Proof-of-Evaluation (PoE) consensus to ensure secure, timely, and energy-efficient task scheduling for IoT networks. TwinChain introduces a closed-loop task offloading technique where DT-based predictive simulation and Proof of Evaluation-based verification are used to ensure secure and efficient task scheduling for IoT networks. The framework starts with task mirroring, which uses digital twin technology to simulate task execution across heterogeneous servers. The Adaptive Evolutionary Twin-based Offloading Scheduler (AETOS) helps each digital twin predictively estimate delay, energy, and trust costs for each possible path. The predicted values are processed using MOFTwin, a federated multi-objective optimizer that computes a global offloading schedule considering capacity and deadline constraints. The offloading schedule is validated using the PoE consensus algorithm and stored as a hashed entry in a distributed ledger managed by digital twin validators. The execution feedback is used to improve the accuracy of digital twin predictions. The simulation results using NS-3, considering 1000 IoT devices and 12 performance metrics, show that TwinChain reduces energy consumption by 21.6%, latency by 29.3%, and achieves an 88.4% task success rate, even at 20% network failures. The simulation results show that TwinChain outperforms six state-of-the-art models while providing scalable trust and reliable offloading for next-generation IoT systems, as envisioned for 6G and cyberphysical systems.
10.1109/tvt.2026.3715448: In low-altitude wireless networks (LAWNs), multi drone delivery operation poses a crucial challenge for advancing the sustainable development in smart cities. However, existing research studies have only tackled either energy consumption or trajectory optimization problems of multi-drones, disregarding the quality of delivery services. To address this problem, we propose a federated edge learning based multi-drone optimal delivery routing approach, aiming to provide optimal delivery paths under realistic route constraints. Specifically, we formulate the optimization problem as a mixed-integer linear programming problem and solve it in a distributed manner. Meanwhile, the utilization of federated edge learning (FEL) method contributes to the accurate prediction in drone delivery travel time. To assess the effectiveness of the proposed model and its constituent parts, we carry out in-depth case studies. Our case studies show that the proposed approach can efficiently achieve the high quality of delivery services in the different scale of LAWNs. Furthermore, it is demonstrated that the distributed approach produces near optimal solutions in low computational time.
10.1109/tia.2026.3714408: Reliable detection of unprecedented anomalies is essential in large scale photovoltaic (PV) plants to prevent potential cascade failures. However, operations and maintenance practices in utility-scale plants are highly optimized, making real anomaly events infrequent and rarely observed. Thus, the recorded PV plant database lacks the information on labeled faults. To overcome this, data from multiple PV sites of several independent producers is aggregated, but privacy concerns limit collaborative learning. To address these limitations, a Reinforcement Federated Learning with Clustering eXpertise (ReFLeCX) framework is proposed for distributed PV anomaly detection. The methodology supports both privacy preservation concerns and provides label-efficient learning. It integrates ramp-rate cluster engineering using deep Q-network augmented by long short-term memory. Reinforcement layer uses optimal classification policies that learn using reward signals derived from clustering metrics and pseudo-labeled anomalies inferred through ramp-rate threshold. The agent is trained locally at each site and federated learning optimizes the aggregated model parameters and updates across sites without transferring raw measurements. The methodology implements FedDyn aggregation strategy to provide robustness under non independent and identically distributed data conditions and mitigate the data distribution drift across temporal changes. Thus, enhancing the global generalization across heterogeneous operating environmental conditions. The proposed ReFLeCX framework is evaluated on real-world multi-site PV datasets, demonstrating improved anomaly separability and cluster coherence. The results prove that the model is suitable for scalable, privacy-aware deployment in industrial PV monitoring systems.
10.1109/tii.2026.3709366: Despite the widespread implementation of various intrusion detection systems (IDSs) in industrial cyber-physical systems (CPS), significant challenges persist, including class imbalance, detection paradox, privacy gap, and arbitrary aggregation. To address these challenges, this article proposes a novel Transformer-based detection with federated privacy-collaborative IDS (TDFP-CIDS) for industrial CPS. First, a Transformer-enhanced external classifier generative adversarial network is designed with Wasserstein distance constraints and label conditioning to stabilize gradient descent, achieving robust semi-supervised classification for class-imbalanced industrial traffic. Second, a hierarchical out-of-distribution detection protocol is proposed to decouple known attack classification and zero-day attack identification into two cascaded stages, resolving the feature entanglement defect of existing single-stage detection frameworks. Third, an adaptive local differential privacy mechanism is integrated into gradient updates to achieve provable privacy guarantees while maintaining detection accuracy. Finally, a decentralized federated distillation scheme is developed to enable architecture-agnostic collaborative training across heterogeneous industrial nodes, realizing the deep integration of knowledge distillation and federated learning without exchanging raw traffic data or model parameters. Experimental results on a real-world industrial CPS dataset show that TDFP-CIDS outperforms state-of-the-art IDS solutions with exceptional detection performance for sparse rare attacks and zero-day attacks.
10.1109/tnse.2026.3716954: Coordinated attacks, such as large-scale scanning, worm outbreaks, and Distributed Denial of Service (DDoS) attacks, exhibit distributed cyberattack characteristics that make them challenging to detect with standalone Intrusion Detection Systems (IDS). Collaborative Intrusion Detection Systems (CIDS) address this limitation by aggregating data from multiple network sources and leveraging collective intelligence for anomaly detection, making them more effective in identifying coordinated attacks. CIDS system employs Ensemble Learning (EL) or Federated Learning (FL) to build robust collaborative anomaly detection. EL enhances detection by integrating predictions from multiple models, while FL enables model aggregation from multiple models and preserves privacy. This research examines the comparative effectiveness of EL and FL within CIDS for robust detection of coordinated attacks in heterogeneous network environments. Benchmarking results reveal that network heterogeneity significantly influences detection model performance. Furthermore, this study provides key insights and lessons learned from the comparative analysis, offering a foundation for future research on cyberattack detection using collaborative anomaly detection methods in CIDS.
10.1109/tdsc.2026.3717223: We present${\sf FedAggVerify}$, a novel single-server federated learning (FL) aggregation protocol and the first to providepublicly verifiable, non-interactiveintegrity proofs for each training round while preserving client-update privacy andparticipation anonymity, even when the aggregator is malicious and colludes with compromised clients. Prior publicly verifiable aggregation schemes either lose soundness under server–client collusion or rely on helper-mediated co-signing and recovery procedures that place an adversarial server on the critical path and create availability and communication bottlenecks.${\sf FedAggVerify}$makes inconsistencies between the accepted client contributions and the released aggregate externally verifiable, supports off-path forensic auditing, and binds released models to the owner through an Error Correction Code-protected signature watermark for intellectual-property protection. We formalize correctness, soundness, client-update indistinguishability, and ownership binding under standard cryptographic assumptions. Experiments using real cryptographic primitives and large model dimensions demonstrate practical efficiency and substantially lower communication, verification, and dropout-recovery overhead than prior publicly verifiable aggregation baselines while maintaining verifiable watermark recovery.
10.1109/tii.2026.3712476: Industrial intrusion detection systems (IIDS) secure industrial networks but need diverse data for training. Data sharing across organizations risks privacy, making centralized learning impractical. Federated learning (FL) enables collaborative training without data exchange but is vulnerable to backdoor attacks. Existing backdoor studies mainly target image-based FL, using visual triggers unsuitable for network data with heterogeneous and semantically sensitive features. Network data differ fundamentally from image pixels, making naive manipulation detectable. Most approaches also rely on multiple attackers or rounds (multishot), and modify labels, ignoring the single-shot, protocol-compliant setting of federated IIDS. We propose context-aware dynamic-trigger backdoor attack, a single-shot and multishot, label-consistent, and protocol-compliant backdoor attack for federated IIDS that shows how a calculated context-aware trigger strategy can easily compromise federated IIDS and highlights the need for stronger defenses. Using lightweight feature adaptation and context-aware trigger generation, CDB attack achieves high attack success and stealth on four IIoT datasets compared with five attacks and five defense baselines, highlighting urgent need for resilient federated defense methods.
10.1109/tdsc.2026.3717085: Federated learning (FL) is increasingly vulnerable to backdoor attacks, where malicious participants inject poisoned updates to implant hidden behaviors within the global model. Existing defenses often rely on ad-hoc aggregation rules, heuristic parameter modifications, or external trusted datasets, severely limiting their robustness, interpretability, and transferability across diverse architectures and attack modalities. To address these fundamental limitations, we propose a Guided Unlearning for Adversarial Robustness and Defense (i.e.,GUARD). It is a unified, data-centric framework, which leverages the principles of machine unlearning to systematically secure FL systems. Specifically,GUARDestablishes a rigorous theoretical link between data influence estimation and backdoor mitigation. It utilizes fast influence-function approximation to efficiently isolate poisoned training contributions without requiring auxiliary clean data. Building on this precise detection, the framework executes a sequential, closed-loop defense pipeline: an influence-guided unlearning stage that explicitly neutralizes malicious parameter biases through reverse optimization, followed by a stability-preserving lightweight fine-tuning stage on internally verified clean data to seamlessly restore standard predictive performance. Comprehensive experiments across diverse datasets, advanced backdoor attacks, and model architectures demonstrate thatGUARDachieves superior threat eradication and clean accuracy preservation compared to state-of-the-art baselines. By transforming backdoor removal into a causally interpretable unlearning process, this work offers a highly robust and principled pathway toward trustworthy FL.
10.1109/tc.2026.3717517: Federated learning (FL) enables collaborations among clients to train machine learning models while protecting their data privacy. Existing FL simulation platforms, designed from the perspectives of traditional distributed training, suffer from laborious code migration between simulation and production, low efficiency, low GPU utility, low scalability with high hardware requirements, and difficulty in simulating stateful clients. In this work, we demystify the challenges and bottlenecks of simulating FL and design a new FL system named FedML Parrot. It improves the training efficiency, remarkably relaxes the hardware requirements, and supports efficient large-scale FL experiments with stateful clients by: (1) sequentially training clients on devices; (2) decomposing original aggregation into local and global aggregation on devices and server respectively; (3) scheduling tasks to mitigate straggler problems and enhance computing utility; (4) distributed client state manager to support various FL algorithms. In addition, built upon our generic APIs and communication interfaces, users can seamlessly transform the simulation into real-world deployment without modifying codes. We evaluate Parrot through extensive experiments for training diverse models on various FL datasets to demonstrate that Parrot can achieve simulating over 1000 clients (stateful or stateless) with flexible GPU device settings (4 ∼ 32) and high GPU utility, 1.2 ∼ 4 times faster than FedScale, and 10 ∼ 100 times memory saving than FedML. And we verify that Parrot works well with homogeneous and heterogeneous devices in three different clusters. Two FL algorithms with stateful clients and four algorithms with stateless clients are simulated to verify the wide adaptability of Parrot to different algorithms.
10.1109/tdsc.2026.3717762: To enhance confidentiality and privacy in Federated Learning (FL) systems, Homomorphic Encryption (HE) is incorporated, which allows the server to aggregate encrypted model updates. However, existing studies have largely overlooked that HE-protected model updates can also be exploited as covert communication channels between colluding malicious clients. This study introduces a novel steganographic mechanism that establishes covert communication channels within FL frameworks secured by the HE algorithm. The proposed method enables colluding clients to embed and transmit hidden messages through model update weights without being detected by the central server or honest participants. To achieve this, we present a spectral-domain embedding technique that adaptively manipulates the magnitude coefficients to encode secret bits while maintaining statistical normality and model integrity. We further design a lightweight server-side defense based on HE-compatible noise injection to disrupt such a covert channel. Comprehensive experiments conducted under representative HE-FL settings with benchmark datasets (MNIST and CIFAR-10) demonstrate the effectiveness and resilience of the proposed attack and defense schemes within the evaluated scenarios. Specifically, our method achieves a high-capacity message embedding of 512 bits per round with nearly zero bit error rate extraction by the receiver in attack scenario. In contrast, under the proposed defense, the bit error rate increases from 0 to 0.17 with Gaussian noise ($std$= 0.1), while reducing the accuracy of the FL model by less than 2%, demonstrating an acceptable mitigation with minimal impact on learning performance.
10.1109/tdsc.2026.3717616: Federated learning (FL) ostensibly safeguards data privacy by sharing only model updates. However, gradient inversion attacks (GIAs) have exposed critical vulnerabilities in this paradigm. While prior literature predominantly assumes a privileged server-side adversary, this work addresses the more insidious and practical threat of client-initiated attacks. Existing client-initiated methodologies remain fragile, treating inversion as a static, single-shot optimization problem that frequently succumbs to catastrophic optimization collapse due to the stochastic nature of FL dynamics. To overcome these limitations, we proposeDCPT(i.e., Diffusion-driven Client-initiated Privacy Theft), a resilient framework that shifts the paradigm toward multi-stage adaptive inversion. Specifically, DCPT integrates a novel adaptive control framework with a closed-loop feedback mechanism, monitoring reconstruction fidelity to dynamically alternate betweenExploitationandExploration, thereby achievingself-correcting. To further guarantee robustness against gradient drift, we incorporate a rolling history constraint fortemporal regularizationand abilevel optimizationfor on-the-fly prior adaptation. Extensive experiments on MNIST and CIFAR-10 demonstrate that DCPT achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction fidelity. Crucially, it also achieves unprecedented multi-round stability and resilience, highlighting the urgent need for advanced defenses against generative client-initiated adversaries.
10.1109/tnse.2026.3717589: Image segmentation is critical in edge computing for real-time medical imaging, surveillance, and autonomous driving—where localized, low-latency processing matters—and federated learning (FL), preserving privacy via local data and enabling collaborative training, is increasingly used to advance it. However, traditional synchronous FL faces challenges in such edge environments, including low communication efficiency, resource waste, and poor model convergence caused by data and device heterogeneity, which limit segmentation performance. To address these issues, we propose AAFLIS, an adaptive asynchronous federated image segmentation framework that integrates momentum acceleration and dynamic coordination mechanisms to achieve efficient and robust distributed training. Specifically, 1) a momentum-based iteration update mechanism is employed to accelerate local model training, effectively overcoming discrepancies in device computing power; 2) the theoretical convergence upper bound under resource constraints is derived, laying a mathematical foundation for algorithm optimization; 3) an optimization model for the number of local iterations under resource constraints is proposed to minimize global loss function. Experimental results show that AAFLIS achieves up to 1221.16% higher Dice score with substantial time and energy savings over baselines under three IID image segmentation settings, and attains a peak Dice improvement of 248.68% on the Non-IID Carvana dataset while likewise reducing computational time and energy resources.
10.1109/tia.2026.3717539: This paper proposes a communication-efficient federated uncertainty-aware Optimal Power Flow (OPF) method with event-triggered federated aggregation for distribution-microgrid coordinated operation under uncertainty. First, we propose a novel federated architecture and uncertainty-aware OPF model, and an event-triggered mechanism is introduced to reduce communication between the distribution network and microgrids while preserving the timeliness of uncertainty representation. Second, we establish a distributed rolling coordination framework for privacy-preserving cross-domain OPF, and introduce a warm-start strategy to reduce repeated iterations and improve online coordination efficiency in adjacent windows. Third, a lightweight feasibility-and-reliability support mechanism with closed-loop safety-margin adaptation and execution-layer affine compensation is developed to enhance online feasibility and reliability under uncertainty, thereby maintaining performance with limited communication and computational overhead. Finally, case studies on the IEEE 33-bus and 69-bus systems demonstrate that, compared with existing methods, the proposed method reduces the total communication volume to 33.3% while maintaining comparable feasibility and reliability performance.
10.1109/tdsc.2026.3717723: Federated Learning (FL) facilitates collaborative model training without sharing local data, yet it grapples with issues of gradient leakage and data heterogeneity. Existing solutions utilize Differentially Private Stochastic Gradient Descent (DP-SGD) to safeguard client model gradients, while the server uses gradient similarity to group and aggregate client models, thereby adapting to diverse data distributions. However, in mixed heterogeneous data environments, FL faces significant challenges due to the coexistence of concept and label distribution shift, which jointly impact client model gradients and render mainstream client grouping methods ineffective. To address this problem, we introduce Decoupled Clustered Federated Learning (DeCFL), a privacy-preserving Clustered Federated Learning (CFL) framework that can disentangle the effects of concept and label distribution shift to enable model grouping. On the client side, we design a gradient-variance-based label distribution metric leveraging noisy gradients to estimate label distributions without incurring additional privacy costs. On the server side, we develop concept-aware clustering using regression residuals from label-to-gradient similarity mapping for precise client grouping. Moreover, we propose a hierarchical aggregation mechanism that assigns aggregation weights to classification layers based on label distributions, thereby reducing the interference of underfitted classes on cluster models. Extensive experiments conducted on MNIST, FMNIST and CIFAR datasets demonstrate that DeCFL performs excellently in mixed heterogeneous environments.
10.1109/tvt.2026.3718162: Establishing and maintaining 5 G mmWave vehicular connectivity poses a challenge due to high user mobility, requiring the design of robust and efficient beam switching procedures. Unlike reactive beam switching based on channel state information (CSI) feedback received from vehicular users, proactive beam switching exploits CSI prediction to prepare in advance for upcoming beam switching decisions. In this paper, we develop a framework forautonomousandself-trainableCSI prediction for mmWave vehicular users. In the proposed framework, base stations (gNBs) collect and label data sets to train a CSI prediction model both independently and using federated learning (FL). The data set combines data extracted from the CSI feedback and cellular vehicle-to-everything (C-V2X) cooperative awareness messages (CAMs) of surrounding vehicles. The framework is placed in the context of machine learning and artificial intelligence (ML/AI)-based Open RAN (O-RAN) applications (rApps and xApps) fed by realistic real-world mobility and CSI data from the DeepMIMO simulator. Detailed evaluation results demonstrate feasibility, accuracy, and flexibility of the proposed CSI prediction framework.
10.1109/tccn.2026.3717832: With the rapid development of the Internet of Things (IoT) and edge computing, the scale and complexity of modern networks have increased significantly, driving the demand for distributed fault diagnosis. Federated learning (FL) effectively addresses the issues of data privacy and dispersion by enabling edge devices to collaboratively train models without sharing raw data. However, existing FL-based fault diagnosis methods still encounter the following challenges. Firstly, static aggregation strategies struggle to balance the contributions of heterogeneous clients dynamically. Secondly, traditional local models are unable to effectively decouple sparse high and low-frequency features in fault signals, thereby limiting the accuracy of fault identification. Finally, the resource constraints of edge devices restrict the deployment of complex diagnostic models. To address these challenges, we propose a federated learning hybrid dynamic weight adjustment method based on delay and model quality, introducing the concept of “accelerated depreciation” in accounting and taxation and the concept of “asset allocation” in economics to improve the communication efficiency of fault diagnosis and reduce the impact of delay differences due to device heterogeneity on the effect of fault diagnosis. Additionally, we propose an adaptive sparse low high frequencies Transformer, introducing a lightweight attention mechanism and an adaptive feature extraction layer, which significantly reduces the computational overhead while maintaining high diagnostic accuracy. The experimental results show that, compared with the most competitive baseline, our method improves the fault diagnosis accuracy by 1% on the Case Western Reserve University Bearing dataset (CWRU), 0.78% on the Xi’an Jiaotong University Gearbox dataset (XJTU), and 0.44% on the Micro service Edge Computing dataset (MICRO).
10.1109/tvt.2026.3718725: Federated learning (FL) is a privacy-preserving distributed training paradigm in which clients collaboratively optimize a global model by periodically synchronizing with a central server. In mobile services, including vehicular networks, clients generate heterogeneous (Non-IID) data under latency and bandwidth constraints. This heterogeneity and dynamic connectivity increase communication overhead. Although local computation can reduce the number of synchronizations, communication still accounts for more than 80% of the total training time. Therefore, communication remains a key bottleneck to the scalability of FL systems. The communication period$\tau$plays a crucial role in the tradeoff between convergence speed and communication efficiency. However, a fixed$\tau$is inherently inflexible. Furthermore, existing adaptive schemes depend on a single historical-loss signal, which delays the mitigation of client gradient conflicts in Non-IID data scenarios. In this paper, we propose Dual-Signal Adaptive Period Control (DS-APC), which adopts a real-time gradient-conflict degree with the loss trend to adjust$\tau$promptly. DS-APC further employs a hybrid attention-based aggregation mechanism that exploits gradient quality and performance indicators. It also incorporates an accuracy-based early-stopping rule for IID settings and a dynamic temperature scheduling strategy for Non-IID settings. Extensive experiments on CIFAR-10, Tiny-ImageNet, STL-10, and SVHN show that, under IID settings, DS-APC improves accuracy over the best baseline by 7.6% on average, and accelerates convergence by reducing training time by about 36% on average. Under Non-IID settings, DS-APC further achieves an average accuracy improvement of 6.6% within fixed time budgets.
10.1109/tce.2026.3718467: Deploying personalized recommender systems on consumer edge devices is impeded by privacy regulations prohibiting centralized data collection and by hardware limits on privacy-preserving computation. Existing federated recommendation approaches either incur prohibitive overhead through cryptographic protocols, suffer from an inherent privacy-utility trade-off via noise-based perturbation, or fail to protect interaction metadata. In response, we propose DAL-FedMF, a privacy-preserving federated matrix factorization framework that breaks this trade-off through a trusted party authority (TPA)-assisted double-anonymization protocol. This protocol enables clients to recover exact global gradients while ensuring the server observes only formally protected updates at minimal computational cost. To accommodate stringent edge resource constraints, we further develop the DAL-FedMF-Light variant via hybrid event-triggered and sparsification mechanisms. Experimental results on three real-world datasets demonstrate that our approach guarantees high recommendation accuracy comparable to non-private baselines, significantly outperforms existing alternatives in efficiency, and provides robust defense against gradient reconstruction and linkage attacks.
10.1109/tdsc.2026.3719352: Security and efficiency are two desirable properties of federated learning (FL). Homomorphic encryption (HE) is widely adopted to enforce data security for FL participants. However, existing solutions based on HE treat FL as a general computation task and apply HE protections indiscriminately at each step without considering FL computations' inherent characteristics, leading to unsatisfactory efficiency. In contrast, we find that the convergence process of FL generally consists of two phases, and the differences between these two phases can be exploited to improve the efficiency of secure FL solutions. In this paper, we propose a secure and fast FL solution named FLSwitch by tailoring different security protections for different learning phases. FLSwitch consists of three novel components, a new secure aggregation protocol based on the Pailliar HE and a residue number coding system outperforming the STATE-of-the-art HE-based solutions, a fast FL aggregation protocol with an extremely light overhead of learning on ciphertexts, and a learning STATE-aware decision model to switch between two protocols during an FL task. Since exploiting FL characteristics is orthogonal to optimizing HE techniques, FLSwitch can be applied to the existing HE-based FL solutions with cutting-edge optimizations, which could further boost secure FL efficiency.
10.1109/tii.2026.3713773: Asynchronous federated learning (AFL) improves the adaptability of federated learning (FL) to dynamic Internet of Vehicles (IoV) environments by reducing communication latency during model aggregation. The inherent network asynchrony of the directed acyclic graph (DAG) blockchain further facilitates the deployment of AFL within IoV. However, the immutability and transparency of blockchain pose critical challenges, such as limited storage capacity at edge nodes and potential privacy leakage of shared model parameters. To address these issues, we propose RBPFL, a novel FL framework that combines redactable blockchain with trusted execution environments (TEEs) by leveraging Intel software guard extension (SGX). The redactable blockchain utilizes a dual-layer architecture, consisting of a model storage layer based on the DAG blockchain and a redaction layer based on the hyperledger Fabric blockchain. The model storage layer stores local and global model updates, while the redaction layer, equipped with SGX-enabled processors, securely executes smart contracts and computes chameleon hash collisions to enable controlled on-chain data redaction. Furthermore, RBPFL employs TEE-based secure aggregation to protect the privacy of model parameters during local model aggregation. Finally, we comprehensively evaluate the performance of the proposed RBPFL framework through experiments with various recurrent neural network (RNN) models and datasets to demonstrate its practical effectiveness.
10.1109/tvt.2026.3719118: Multimodal federated learning (MFL) over wireless links faces significant challenges due to limited bandwidth, heterogeneous client resources, and non-IID data distributions. In this paper, we propose a semantic-aware multi-agent bandit (SMAB) scheduling framework for wireless MFL, which jointly performs client selection and channel assignment based on compact semantic features instead of full model updates. To quantify the utility of local data, we introduce three semantic metrics, namely coverage, diversity, and contribution potential. Moreover, long-term participation constraints are adopted to replace rigid per-round selection requirements, thereby improving both fairness and scheduling flexibility. The proposed SMAB algorithm combines upper confidence bound (UCB)-based exploration with Lyapunov virtual queues to balance latency minimization, client participation fairness, and energy constraints. Experimental results on a custom multimodal MNIST–AudioMNIST benchmark show that SMAB significantly reduces training latency while maintaining or improving model accuracy compared with random and round-robin baselines. These results demonstrate that the proposed framework provides an effective trade-off between communication efficiency and learning performance in resource-constrained wireless MFL systems.
10.1109/tnse.2026.3719127: Fusing digital twins (DTs) with world models (WMs) promises a leap from reactive monitoring to proactive control. However, deploying high-fidelity WMs faces a fundamental cognitive gap: the immense computational demand of foundation models conflicts with the resource constraints of 6G edge nodes, while privacy regulations hinder the centralization of raw sensory data required for training. To bridge this gap, this paper presents HongAvg, a hierarchical on-demand cognitive split federated learning framework designed as cognitive infrastructure for next-generation DTs. By establishing a national-basin-edge three-tier architecture, HongAvg introduces foundation models to resource-constrained edges via split computing, offloading heavy cognitive reasoning while preserving data privacy. We propose a dual-stream semantic consistency mechanism to align edge interactions with the foundation model's cognition, ensuring that distributed cognitive primitives serve as valid inputs for global state estimation. Validated on a heterogeneous benchmark, HongAvg serves as a prototype for industrial cognitive computing, improving accuracy in visual monitoring by up to 8.9% and reducing edge memory usage by approximately 75%. This work provides the scalable architectural prerequisite necessary for evolving static DTs into proactive WM-driven multi-agent orchestrated intelligent systems.
10.1109/tce.2026.3719763: Smart-home consumer electronics (CE) sharded blockchains face a configuration dilemma: node-resource information is scattered across home gateways, while shard configuration requires global coordination. Centralized optimization exposes local resource states, making it difficult to balance real-time performance and security-related risk exposure. To address this problem, this paper proposes FedShard-DES, a FedPareto-driven double-elite-selection framework for federated multi-objective optimization of sharded blockchain configuration. The proposed model jointly optimizes shard failure probability, transaction throughput, decentralization entropy, and consensus latency. In FedShard-DES, each CE client locally performs double-elite-selection evolutionary search and uploads only its Pareto archive instead of raw node-resource data.
